```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)
library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr); library(ggplot2)
library(stringr); library(forcats); library(scales)
```

> **Important note about the data.** The file `data.csv` is the WHO country-level cholera table
> (one row = one country in one year, 1949-2016). It is **not** a line list of individual patients,
> so it has **no Age and no Sex columns**. Where the exam asks for age groups or sex, this report
> explains what is not possible and uses the closest available grouping (WHO Region, Country, Year).
> A ready-to-use template for a real line list is given in the Appendix.

# 1. Import and first look

```{r import}
raw <- read_csv("data.csv", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
names(raw)
dim(raw)
head(raw)
```

The dataset has **`r nrow(raw)` observations** and **`r ncol(raw)` variables**
(Country, Year, Number of reported cases, Number of reported deaths, Case fatality rate, WHO Region).

# 2. Q1: Identify data quality issues

```{r quality}
d <- raw %>%
  rename(country = Country, year = Year, cases = `Number of reported cases of cholera`,
         deaths = `Number of reported deaths from cholera`,
         cfr = `Cholera case fatality rate`, region = `WHO Region`)

# 1. Missing values
colSums(is.na(d))

# 2. Non-numeric text hiding in numeric columns
non_numeric <- function(x) !is.na(x) & is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)))
d %>% filter(non_numeric(cases) | non_numeric(deaths) | non_numeric(cfr))

# 3. Duplicates (same country and year)
sum(duplicated(d[, c("country", "year")]))

# 4. Logical errors after conversion
d_num <- d %>% mutate(across(c(year, cases, deaths, cfr), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))
d_num %>% filter(deaths > cases)                                   # deaths > cases
d_num %>% filter(!is.na(cases), cases > 0, !is.na(deaths), !is.na(cfr),
                 abs(deaths / cases * 100 - cfr) > 0.1)             # CFR does not match
d_num %>% filter(cfr > 100)                                        # impossible CFR
d_num %>% filter(cases == 0, !is.na(cfr))                          # CFR with zero cases
```

**Issues found**

1. **Missing values** in cases, deaths and CFR.
2. **Text in numeric columns**: `"Unknown"` (Germany 2016) and a corrupted entry `"3 5"`, `"0 0"`, `"0.0 0.0"` (Iraq 2016).
3. **Impossible value**: Italy 1998 has 2 cases, 9 deaths and CFR 450% (deaths are greater than cases).
4. **CFR that does not match** deaths / cases (for example Zimbabwe 2009, and several 2005 records with CFR 0 despite deaths).
5. **Zero-case rows** that still carry a CFR.
6. **Gaps in years** per country (surveillance is not continuous), so totals across countries are not comparable year to year.
7. Extreme skew and outliers (a few huge epidemics, for example India, Haiti and Peru dominate the totals).

# 3. Q2 and Q3: Harmonise Sex and recode Age

The dataset contains **no `Sex` and no `Age` variable**, so these steps cannot be done here.
The equivalent harmonisation done on this file is **cleaning the numeric columns and recoding the
`Year` into periods**, which plays the role of the age-group variable in the later analysis.

```{r clean}
clean <- d %>%
  mutate(
    cases  = ifelse(non_numeric(cases),  NA, as.numeric(cases)),
    deaths = ifelse(non_numeric(deaths), NA, as.numeric(deaths)),
    year   = as.numeric(year),
    region = str_squish(region)
  ) %>%
  select(-cfr) %>%                               # recompute CFR ourselves
  filter(!(country == "Italy" & year == 1998)) %>%   # impossible record (deaths > cases)
  mutate(
    cfr = ifelse(!is.na(cases) & cases > 0 & !is.na(deaths), deaths / cases * 100, NA),
    period = cut(year, breaks = c(1948, 1969, 1989, 1999, 2009, 2016),
                 labels = c("1949-1969", "1970-1989", "1990-1999", "2000-2009", "2010-2016"))
  )

cat("Rows kept:", nrow(clean), "\n")
table(clean$period)
```

# 4. Q4: Statistical analyses for the Minister

## 4a. Total cases and geographic distribution

```{r total}
total_cases <- sum(clean$cases, na.rm = TRUE)
total_cases

by_region <- clean %>% group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(cases = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE), deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_cases = round(cases / sum(cases) * 100, 1)) %>% arrange(desc(cases))
by_region

top_countries <- clean %>% group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(cases = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE), deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(cases)) %>% slice_head(n = 10)
top_countries
```

## 4b. Deaths and case fatality rate (CFR = deaths / cases x 100)

```{r cfr}
# Use only rows where BOTH cases and deaths are known, so the CFR is not biased
known <- clean %>% filter(!is.na(cases), !is.na(deaths))
overall <- known %>% summarise(cases = sum(cases), deaths = sum(deaths),
                               CFR_percent = round(deaths / cases * 100, 2))
overall

cfr_region <- known %>% group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), deaths = sum(deaths), CFR_percent = round(deaths / cases * 100, 2),
            .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(desc(CFR_percent))
cfr_region
```

## 4c. Most and least affected groups (replacing age groups)

Age groups are not in the file, so we rank **WHO Regions** and **periods**.

```{r affected}
by_region %>% slice(c(1, n()))        # most and least affected region
clean %>% group_by(period) %>% summarise(cases = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct = round(cases / sum(cases) * 100, 1))
```

*Highlight on children:* not possible with this dataset (no age). See the Appendix for the code to use on a line list.

## 4d. Gender distribution

Not possible (no `Sex` variable). See the Appendix.

## 4e. Are cases equal across groups? (chi-square goodness-of-fit)

H0: cases are equally distributed. H1: they are not.

```{r chisq}
chisq.test(by_region$cases)                       # across WHO regions
period_tot <- clean %>% group_by(period) %>% summarise(x = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull(x)
chisq.test(period_tot)                            # across periods
country_tot <- clean %>% group_by(country) %>% summarise(x = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull(x)
chisq.test(country_tot)                           # across countries
```

With p-values far below 0.05 we **reject H0**: cases are **not** equally distributed across regions,
periods or countries. (With counts this large, any difference is "significant", so look at the size
of the differences in the tables above.)

## 4f. Epidemic curve (cases per year)

```{r curve}
yearly <- clean %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(cases = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE), deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(yearly, aes(year, cases)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Epidemic curve: reported cholera cases per year", x = "Year", y = "Reported cases")
yearly %>% arrange(desc(cases)) %>% slice_head(n = 5)
```

## 4g. Distribution by outcome and recovery rate

The file has deaths only, so **survived = cases - deaths**, and the recovery rate is a proxy.

```{r outcome}
out <- known %>% summarise(Died = sum(deaths), Survived = sum(cases - deaths)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2))
out
```

# 5. Q5: Figures

```{r figs}
ggplot(by_region, aes(fct_reorder(region, cases), cases, fill = region)) + geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Reported cases by WHO region", x = NULL, y = "Cases")

ggplot(top_countries, aes(fct_reorder(country, cases), cases)) + geom_col(fill = "firebrick") +
  coord_flip() + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Top 10 countries by reported cases", x = NULL, y = "Cases")

ggplot(cfr_region, aes(fct_reorder(region, CFR_percent), CFR_percent)) + geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  coord_flip() + labs(title = "Case fatality rate by WHO region", x = NULL, y = "CFR (%)")

clean %>% group_by(year, region) %>% summarise(cases = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, cases, colour = region)) + geom_line() + scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Cases per year by WHO region", x = "Year", y = "Cases", colour = "Region")
```

# 6. Q6: Risk factors driving the outbreak

With country-year data the "risk factors" are **region, period and country burden**. Because deaths
out of cases is a count out of a total, we use a **binomial (logistic) regression** and report
**odds ratios** for dying.

```{r model}
m_dat <- known %>% filter(deaths <= cases, cases > 0) %>%
  mutate(region = relevel(factor(region), ref = "Europe"))

fit <- glm(cbind(deaths, cases - deaths) ~ region + period, data = m_dat, family = binomial)
summary(fit)

est <- exp(cbind(OR = coef(fit), confint.default(fit)))
round(est, 2)
```

**How to read:** OR above 1 = higher odds of dying than the reference group (Europe, 1949-1969);
OR below 1 = lower; a 95% interval containing 1 = not significant.
Because the data are overdispersed (countries differ a lot), treat the p-values as indicative.

# 7. Q7: Recommendations

1. **Fix reporting quality**: standard templates, mandatory numeric fields, validation (deaths cannot exceed cases), and no free-text such as "Unknown".
2. **Collect line-list data** (age, sex, district, onset date, outcome) so children and gender can be analysed.
3. **Focus resources on the highest-burden regions and countries** shown in the tables.
4. **Reduce deaths where CFR is high** (above the 1% WHO target): ORS and IV fluids, treatment centres, trained staff.
5. **Strengthen early detection**: rapid reporting, active case finding, lab confirmation.
6. **WASH and prevention**: safe water, sanitation, hygiene promotion and oral cholera vaccination in hotspots.
7. **Fill surveillance gaps**: many country-years are missing, so under-reporting is likely.

# Appendix: template for a real line list (Age and Sex)

Use this if your exam file has columns `age`, `sex`, `outcome`, `district` (set `eval = TRUE`).

```{r appendix, eval=FALSE}
df <- df %>%
  mutate(sex = str_to_lower(str_trim(sex)),
         sex = case_when(sex %in% c("m", "male", "1") ~ "Male",
                         sex %in% c("f", "female", "2") ~ "Female", TRUE ~ NA_character_),
         age_group = cut(age, breaks = c(-Inf, 4, 14, 24, 49, Inf),
                         labels = c("<5", "5-14", "15-24", "25-49", "50+")))
df %>% count(age_group) %>% mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))
df %>% count(sex) %>% mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))
chisq.test(table(df$age_group)); chisq.test(table(df$sex)); chisq.test(table(df$district))
df$died <- ifelse(df$outcome == "Died", 1, 0)
m <- glm(died ~ age_group + sex + district, data = df, family = binomial)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(m), confint.default(m)))
```
